properties.name: review_relations can say a contradiction supports, and 10 corroborations stored as conflicts are corrected
properties.rationale:
The finding (fact:root-cause-review-relations-cannot-mark-a-contradiction-supporting-and-the-default-says-opposing-2026-10-13) traced it to the writer, not the detector: review_relations' per-link request accepted only relation, other_type, other_id, evidence, incoming, other_design and other_name, refused anything else, and relate.rs wrote only `evidence`; schema/inference.yaml declares CONTRADICTS alignment with default opposing, which materialises on create. So a writer who meant corroboration had no field to say it, put it in the evidence, and the stored edge asserted the opposite. The 2026-07-28 detector fix (heal.rs skips supporting) could not help, and is left unchanged.

Fixed at the class rather than the instance. The defaulted set is read from the schema per relation (relate::review_link_properties), so CAUSES' basis and validation_status, DUPLICATES' basis and DEPENDS_ON's optional and weight_basis became sayable in the same change as alignment. Nothing is inferred from evidence text. Additive: every new field is optional, no existing argument, refusal or reply shape changed for a caller who does not use them, and the two toolsnaps that moved (review_relations, add_decision) only gained fields and a description sentence. A value for an edge already stored is refused rather than reported as already present, because "already present" would tell the writer their corroboration landed while the edge still says opposing; the refusal names create_edge as the deliberate way to restate it.

The guard against recurrence is every_defaulted_edge_property_is_exposed_or_exempt.rs: every tool writers.json maps to an edge type, plus add_decision, must expose each defaulted property of each edge it draws or name it in EXEMPT with a reason. It found no other unexplained gap on the typed helpers; the seven exemptions are weight_basis on five helpers that set no weight, depends_on's optional (left open, same class), and violates_rule's status (born proposed). Tests were committed first and seen failing on main (5090b58c6), then passing on the fix (12c543617).

The record correction was made on flo2.io with the tools 0.83.5 serves: review_relations re-drawing an existing edge reports it already present and changes nothing, so each edge was restated with create_edge (which replaces an edge's properties) carrying alignment supporting and its stored evidence again; the evidence was compared byte for byte against the export taken before. Which route drew each of the 10 originally is not recorded on an edge, so "drawn through review_relations" stays inferred from the evidence wording, as the finding said.

Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: A review link now takes an optional field for each property its relation's schema gives a default: `alignment` (CONTRADICTS), `basis` (CAUSES and DUPLICATES), `validation_status` (CAUSES), `optional` and `weight_basis` (DEPENDS_ON), on review_relations' links and add_decision's related_to. relate.rs writes what the link says; absent stores the default exactly as before. A value the schema does not allow, a property the relation does not declare, and a value that differs from an edge already stored are refused naming what is legal. A conformance test holds every typed edge tool to the same rule, with seven reasoned exemptions. In this design, the 10 CONTRADICTS edges whose evidence says "alignment=supporting" were restated as supporting through create_edge with their evidence byte for byte; detect_defects went from 42 contradictions to 33 (135 defects to 126), and the 83 other CONTRADICTS edges are untouched.
